claims.evidence: The witness report explicitly states the capacity in kilograms is not shown.
The witness identifies the items as gas cylinders.

risks.risk: The cylinders may be expired or past their re-qualification date, making them illegal or dangerous to refill.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the manufacture or expiry date stamped on the collar/shroud.
risks.if_unproven: as expired units valued for scrap metal

risks.risk: The valve threads or seals may be damaged, leading to leaks.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the valve assembly and internal threads.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a full valve replacement

risks.risk: The actual capacity may be smaller than 12.5kg (e.g., 6kg or 10kg).
risks.proof: A photo of the stamped capacity (kg) on the cylinder collar.
risks.if_unproven: as the smallest standard size visible

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the stamped text on the collar showing the manufacture/expiry date.
Photo of the stamped capacity (e.g., 12.5kg) and Tare Weight (TW).
Clear photo of the valve opening to inspect the threads.
response.reason: The items are identified as gas cylinders, but the absence of expiry dates and capacity stamps requires them to be priced at their lowest utility or scrap value.
